subject: modelling observer bias at point counts

messages.author: 718b613c6c07389a
messages.subject: modelling observer bias at point counts
parts:
Dear mailing list,

I am working on a project that involves a distance sampling spotlight
survey of mammals around the south-west of the UK, using variable
circular plots. We have carried out several thousand point counts in
varying conditions, with different observers. I am interested in
investigating the effects of these factors i.e. observer, weather, time
of night etc. on the frequency of observations of the different
species. The frequency data for all species have poisson distributions,
with a large number of zeros (i.e. no observations at a point count). I
was thinking of using a generalised linear model (GLM), with individual
point counts as the sampling unit. However, we are quantifying the
effort at each point by taking the proportion of 360 degrees that has an
unobstructed view over the surrounding habitat. I'm not sure how to
analyse the data once it is standardised for effort at each point. Can
I still carry out a GLM in some shape or form? Any suggestions would be
gratefully received.

Many thanks,

John Davison
j.da...@csl.gov.uk
